svg.title: A cut pause ends the relay itself, and the form decides how the client retries
svg.desc: A gate file declaring paused true and cut true reaches a relay already in flight. The router cancels the upstream request in both forms. In the default close form it closes the client connection with no terminal chunk, so the client retries once as a streaming request with a byte-identical body. In the error form it writes an event: error carrying overloaded_error and then ends the stream, so the client retries once as a non-streaming request. Either way the retry waits in the paused FIFO and resume admits it in arrival order.
svg.text: One cut, two client-visible forms
the gate file router-gate.json is written while a generation relay is already in flight
{ "paused": true, "cut": true }
{ "cut_form": "close" | "error" }
the relay polls the gate file, so a cut reaches relays already streaming
and survives a router restart: nothing is carried in memory
cut_form: "close" — the default
cut_form: "error"
relay in flight
engine streaming; client has some content
the router ends it
cancels the upstream read, closes the upstream request
client connection closed, no terminal chunk
the response never ends cleanly, so the turn cannot be read as complete
client retries once
same conversation, streaming, byte-identical body
relay in flight
engine streaming; client has some content
the router ends it the same way
cancels the upstream read, closes the upstream request
event: error carrying overloaded_error
then the stream ends cleanly, so the client has an explicit signal
client retries once
same conversation, but as a non-streaming request (stream:false)
either retry waits in the paused FIFO
no new generation is admitted while paused; resume admits the held and retried requests in arrival order, exactly as a pause without a cut drains today
the cut is a property of the pause: cut alone ends nothing, so a relay cannot be cut on admission and loop
